issue_context.title: Sensors created by Tesla Powerwall not shown in energy dashboard
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The Tesla Powerwall integration creates sensors for each of the following:

1. Energy being pulled from or returned to the grid
2. Energy being pulled from or returned to your battery
3. Energy being consumed by your house
4. Energy being generated by your solar panels

These seem like obvious choices for what I would want to select in the new energy dashboard but currently they do not appear. According to [this](https://www.home-assistant.io/more-info/statistics/) that is a bug so wanted to report it.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.8.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

One thing that's a bit odd with this integration currently is the sensors it creates to track grid and battery energy usage can have a positive or negative value. Positive if you are pulling energy from it, negative if you are returning energy to it.

The energy dashboard seems to want me to enter one entity tracking how much energy I am pulling from the grid and one tracking how much entity I am returning to the grid. Not sure if it will work with one sensor that can be both positive and negative, might have to be split into two.

Have just looked at this myself now we have the new energy dashboard.

I think the main issue is that the data you want are actually attributes and not sensors?

I tried adding them as sensors via templates in configuration but still no joy. I think the integration needs some modifications to present various items as extra sensors to provide the kWh totals?

```yaml
sensor:
  - platform: template
    sensors:
      powerwall_site_import:
        friendly_name: "Powerwall Site Import"
        value_template: "{{ state_attr('sensor.powerwall_site_now','energy_imported_(in_kW)')}}"
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        unique_id: "f7132181-0631-4723-b489-655476e36079"
        device_class: energy
      powerwall_site_export:
        friendly_name: "Powerwall Site Export"
        value_template: "{{ state_attr('sensor.powerwall_site_now','energy_exported_(in_kW)')}}"
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        unique_id: "ee708a3d-1d6f-45cf-b474-2d6d93c4b9f1"
        device_class: energy
      powerwall_solar_generated:
        friendly_name: "Powerwall Solar Generated"
        value_template: "{{ state_attr('sensor.powerwall_solar_now','energy_exported_(in_kW)')}}"
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        unique_id: "4092866e-b26d-4041-be58-8f3319823323"
        device_class: energy
```
Use the integration integration to convert them to be usable for energy

> Use the integration integration to convert them to be usable for energy

The kWh totals exist, just only as attributes currently. No need to integrate the instantaneous values to produce a slightly less accurate version of something that already exists?

> > Use the integration integration to convert them to be usable for energy
> 
> The kWh totals exist, just only as attributes currently. No need to integrate the instantaneous values to produce a slightly less accurate version of something that already exists?

Yes, but this will make it usable now as opposed to later when someone does the work to convert the sensors.

Here's the config that I used to get working sensors.
```yaml
platform: template
sensors:
  grid_import:
    value_template: "{{state_attr('sensor.powerwall_site_now', 'energy_exported_(in_kW)')}}"
  
    unit_of_measurement: kWh
    device_class: energy
    attribute_templates:
      last_reset: '1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'
      state_class: 'measurement'
  grid_export:
    value_template: "{{state_attr('sensor.powerwall_site_now', 'energy_imported_(in_kW)')}}"
  
    unit_of_measurement: kWh
    device_class: energy
    attribute_templates:
      last_reset: '1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'
      state_class: 'measurement'
  solar_production:
    value_template: "{{state_attr('sensor.powerwall_solar_now', 'energy_exported_(in_kW)')}}"
  
    unit_of_measurement: kWh
    device_class: energy
    attribute_templates:
      last_reset: '1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'
      state_class: 'measurement'
```
I've previously created an issue #53944 to resolve issues with some of the units of this integration but this approach may be required to get it to work with HA Energy.
I've also created another issue for HA Energy battery support #54008.

Oh neat, I didn't realize that was all there was to it. So adding `last_reset` and `state_class: measurement` to making a sensor is the key to making it available for use in the energy dashboard. For others that are interested and we're also confused looking at that config, notes on why these fields are important in this discussion can be found [here](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor).

Looks like bdraco is already working on a non-workaround fix though so can also just wait if your need isn't urgent.
